note: Every production-readiness item, each with the command that decides it. NS16 runs them in the sandbox; an item without a command is refused when the checklist is written. {placeholders} are filled from the project; $VARIABLES are the owner's, never written here.

items.title: The application starts and answers on its port and health route
items.why: A release that does not start, or starts on the wrong port, is caught before a user finds it.

items.title: It builds from a clean checkout
items.why: A release is only as reproducible as its build from the repository alone.

items.title: The behaviour lock passes: the features still do what they did
items.why: The safety net EAOS wrote before any change is the definition of 'nothing broke'.

items.title: No known high or critical vulnerability, and no committed secret
items.why: A release carrying a published vulnerability is an incident waiting for a date.

items.title: The fast checks pass on every file
items.why: The checks every commit runs must also hold for the whole tree.

items.title: Rolling back one commit leaves a working application
items.command: git checkout --detach HEAD~1 && {build} && {safety_net}; status=$?; git checkout -; exit $status
items.why: A rollback that has never been tried is a hope, not a plan.

items.title: The database can be backed up and the backup restores
items.command: pg_dump "$DATABASE_URL" -Fc -f readiness.dump && pg_restore --list readiness.dump > /dev/null && pg_restore -d "$RESTORE_DATABASE_URL" --clean --if-exists readiness.dump
items.why: A backup is proven only by a restore.

items.title: The database file can be backed up and the copy is intact
items.command: sqlite3 "$DATABASE_PATH" ".backup readiness-backup.db" && sqlite3 readiness-backup.db "PRAGMA integrity_check" | grep -qx ok
items.why: A backup is proven only by reading it back.

items.title: The CI workflow runs locally
items.why: A pipeline that only runs on the server is debugged on the server.
